headline: Medium-risk pair: Plane can ingest Dagster-produced content, creating prompt-injection and data-leakage pathways; no direct shared-write conflict is documented.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Dagster has no direct I/O surfaces or shared channel, but Plane accepts file uploads and hyperlinks, so Dagster-generated artifacts could be copied into Plane and treated as content. That makes an injection pathway plausible in default workflows, though not proven. Dagster’s lack of clipboard/MCP/network reduces direct bridging; Plane’s permissive content surfaces keep the risk above low.
conditions: IF Dagster outputs are manually pasted or uploaded into Plane
IF Plane interprets uploaded text or linked content as instructions
mitigations: Disable copy/paste of generated task text into Plane
Use a review-only step before importing Dagster artifacts
Strip instructions from uploaded files before upload
requires-engineering: add provenance labels to imported content

B_data_leakage.rationale: Dagster touches no data classes and has no network egress, but Plane handles files, images, notes, and hyperlinks and has broad network egress. If sensitive pipeline artifacts from Dagster are uploaded into Plane, they can leave the local boundary through Plane’s external calls. The pairwise leakage path is plausible even though the exact data flow is not documented.
conditions: IF Dagster artifacts contain sensitive operational data
IF those artifacts are uploaded into Plane or linked from Plane
mitigations: Block sensitive uploads into Plane
Redact secrets from Dagster outputs before sharing
Restrict Plane projects to non-sensitive data
requires-engineering: enforce DLP on file uploads

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Dagster cannot write the filesystem or modify git state, while Plane also lacks filesystem write in the profile. With no overlapping write authority, the classic shared-write conflict is absent. Plane can support multiple instances, but Dagster’s read/write restrictions make contention unlikely and the blast radius small.
conditions: IF an external orchestrator grants both agents write access outside the profiles
IF a shared mutable resource is introduced by deployment
mitigations: Keep both agents on separate workspaces
Avoid granting shared write credentials
Run Plane in isolated projects
requires-engineering: add resource locking for shared backends

D_cascading_error.rationale: Dagster produces data-engineering outputs that Plane can store as tasks, notes, or hyperlinks. Plane may then treat imported content as authoritative work items, so an error in Dagster can cascade into planning or scheduling mistakes. Plane’s multiple-instance support and broad content surfaces increase the chance of propagation, though no direct automation is shown.
conditions: IF Dagster output is imported into Plane without human verification
IF Plane users act on imported tasks or notes as authoritative
mitigations: Require human review before creating Plane tasks from Dagster output
Mark imported items as untrusted
Separate generated facts from action items
requires-engineering: add validation gates before task creation

E_compliance.rationale: No residency, certification, or retention mismatch is documented in either profile, and Dagster touches no data classes. Plane does handle files and notes, so compliance concerns are possible only if regulated data is introduced into Plane. Because the other agent is not a compliance source here, the risk stays low and is driven by Plane’s broader data handling.
conditions: IF regulated data is stored in Plane
IF retention or deletion policies differ between the deployment and the data owner
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of Plane
Document retention settings for Plane
Limit uploads to non-sensitive artifacts
requires-engineering: align retention and deletion workflows
